sections.title: The letter eme
paragraphs: You call this letter (eme) /ˈɛmi/. Its main sound is heard in the word (mão) /ˈmɐ̃w̃/, which means hand. This letter has two different sounds.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: Press your lips tightly together and turn on your voice. Send all the air out through your nose. For the other sound, keep your lips open and do not close your mouth. Send the air through your nose and mouth together. Put two fingers against your nose to feel it buzz.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: At the start of a syllable, the letter is pronounced with closed lips. You hear this sound in (mãe) /ˈmɐ̃j̃/. At the end of a syllable, the letter is not pronounced as a separate sound. Instead, it changes the vowel before it into a nasal vowel. A nasal vowel is a vowel where air goes out through the nose and the mouth at the same time. You hear this in (fim) /ˈfĩ/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: At the end of words, do not press your lips together like in team. Keep your mouth open and let air flow through your nose. Touch the sides of your nose to make sure it shakes without closing your lips.
